title: Simulation Framework and Optimization of Superconducting Transmon-Tunable Coupler-Transmon System for Qudit Gates
problem: Superconducting quantum processors are limited by low qubit counts and high gate errors; extending to qudits offers larger state space but requires optimization for qutrit-based systems.
motivation: Optimizing qudit-based quantum processors can improve gate fidelities and move toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: An integrated simulation framework predicts cross-Kerr interactions in TTT systems and fidelities of two-qutrit CPhase gates under noise. Control-device co-optimization identifies conditions maximizing target frequency in adiabatic schemes to achieve higher gate fidelity.
key_novelty: Simulation framework for predicting and optimizing qutrit gate fidelities in superconducting TTT systems.
contributions: Integrated simulation framework for TTT cross-Kerr interactions
Noise-aware qutrit CPhase gate fidelity prediction
Identification of conditions for maximum adiabatic target frequency
limitations: Framework validation limited to reported TTT systems; generalization to other qudit platforms requires further study.
